People keep asking if building in public is dead. Most of my work on Calmly Crashing this month is writing filled-in examples for printable pages, and nobody would call that exciting.

I'm posting it anyway, because the boring middle is the part I always want to see from other people.

patterns: The notebook too nice to write in showed up twice from unrelated accounts in one day. Admitting you're scared to ruin the page is a shared joke, and it sits right on the Smaller Start Kit's no-blank-page idea.
Big-account energy today is about attention, not tools: Dan Koe's 'your only competition is your own mind' (~115k) and James Clear's path of least resistance (~63k).
Executive dysfunction is the day's most common self-description, almost always as a one-line joke. Gentle, specific replies stand out more than advice.
'Is building in public dead?' came up from several small founders. Posts about the boring middle of the work are an open lane.
Fountain pen talk is playful and messy today (ink on faces, first 'real' pens, comic art in fountain pen ink), not reviews.
Warning sign: Yongfook (175k) says he'll block AI-sounding replies, and that post drew 62 replies. Every reply has to read like a person with a real question.

reply_ideas.description: a joke about buying a notebook because the paper feels nice, then refusing to write in it because your handwriting isn't worthy of the pages
reply_ideas.reply_text: What if the first page is a grocery list on purpose? Once it says "buy eggs" in your worst handwriting, there's nothing left to ruin. I'm curious whether the nicest-paper notebooks ever get used at all, or if they just get admired.

reply_ideas.description: Toby Shorin announcing an evening on Wendell Berry's life and work next Friday, with zines of favorite pieces and short readings
reply_ideas.reply_text: Berry wrote by hand and made a whole essay out of refusing to buy a computer, so zines feel like exactly the right format for an evening about him. Which piece are you most hoping a newcomer picks up first?

reply_ideas.description: a researcher who finally digitized their old Hindustani classical music notebook from 2012, messy multilingual handwriting and all
reply_ideas.reply_text: I love that the handwriting and the 2012 transliterations made it through. Did you keep the messy scan next to the clean version? In a music notebook the scribbles in the margins are sometimes the only record of how you were actually being taught.

bip_draft:
The Smaller Start Kit is the first thing going into the Calmly Crashing shop. It's a set of paper pages for days when everything feels like too much, and every page comes with a filled-in example so you never have to start on a blank one.

The shop isn't open yet, but it's close.

#buildinpublic
video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. Overhead on textured cream paper, a hand opens a brand-new notebook and writes 'buy eggs' in loose, messy handwriting at the top of the first page, then turns to page two and keeps writing. Pen and paper sounds only, no music. End on a card that reads 'Now it's yours.' Pairs with the nice-notebook post.

x_posts.title: The notebook on the shelf
x_posts.text:
Is there a nice notebook on your shelf that you're saving for when your handwriting gets better?

I think the notebook would rather have your messy handwriting today than stay perfect on a shelf for another year.
